top.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
top.description: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage. With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington. The 80-year-old Republican heads to the ASEAN summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate. Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage. “After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset,” Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) told a news briefing. – Iran, trade, China – That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics. China has described the midterms as an “internal affair” and said it is “willing to continue working” with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress. But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders’ radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations. “In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved,” Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month. “The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States’ Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump’s decision-making on the issue will become more predictable.” Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the United States and Iran is unlikely. A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration’s “soft approach” to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia. Leaders in the world’s largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump’s barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports. Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy. The Democrats will not get an easy ride in undoing Trump’s policies, though. The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation — which he has vowed to use. – High-profile meeting – Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. top.title: Chelsea defender Malo Gusto ‘assessing his options’ ahead of January transfer window — report
top.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Malo Gusto of Chelsea acknowledges the fans after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on October 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Chris Lee - Chelsea FC/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) | Chelsea FC via Getty Images We’re slowly approaching the January transfer window, and given that it’s the international break, there’s plenty of space for a few rumors to make their way around the footballverse. Of particular interest to us may be the story that Malo Gusto is said to be “open” to leaving Chelsea and is now “assessing his options” with three and half years still to run on his current contract (2030 expiry). The BBC are among those who nibbled a bit at this little rumor-nugget, adding that while Chelsea’s stance at the moment is “unclear”, we were shopping the 23-year-old around this summer already, at a £75m asking price. That’s a rather optimistic valuation, especially now that Manchester City cannot just make up income numbers (or can they?). Enzo Maresca was always a big fan of Gusto, and a reunion was speculated about before the season, but unlike in the case of Enzo Fernández, did not come to fruition. It probably won’t help Gusto’s valuation that he’s finding himself less and less involved as the season’s come along. He’s not started a league match for two months, and I don’t imagine too many are questioning those decisions from Xabi Alonso, unlike some of his other choices of late. Gusto’s substitute appearance against Sunderland was his 100th Premier League appearance, and 144th overall for Chelsea. He’s among our longest-serving players these days despite his young age — a testament to the constant chopping and changing of the team. Only Reece James and Wesley Fofana have been part of the first-team squad for longer. But throughout those 3.5 years, Gusto has failed to convince consistently, despite his versatility and world class speed. He’s had moments of great impact and could at times even be practically unplayable for the opposition with his fluid movement and lack of a defined position. But those moments have been few and far between. His best season for us was, perhaps, his very first, when he often thrived in Mauricio Pochettino’s chaosball. Since Poch is about to take over at Manchester United, perhaps they will be interested in another Chelsea castoff? Malo Gusto is open to a move away in January. The France international hasn't started a PL match in nearly two months. His view has been amicably communicated internally. Chelsea valued him at £75m in the summer. https://t.co/N1MV5mdfXE — Nizaar Kinsella (@NizaarKinsella) November 11, 2026

top.title: Hansi Flick achieves remarkable La Liga record as Barcelona dominate title race
top.description: Hansi Flick achieves remarkable La Liga record as Barcelona dominate title race Hansi Flick has established an extraordinary level of consistency in La Liga, spending 68 of the 88 matchdays he has overseen as Barcelona manager at the top of the table. According to figures published by AS , the German has occupied first place for approximately 77% of his league tenure, placing him among the most successful Barcelona managers in the competition’s history. His dominance has coincided with two consecutive La Liga titles in 2024/25 and 2025/26, and now, with Barcelona also leading the 2026/27 standings after 12 matches, Flick is positioning himself for another championship. Flick’s La Liga dominance puts him among Barcelona’s greats The outlet affirms that of the 88 league matchdays under his management, his team have finished in first place on 68 occasions, leaving just 20 matchdays in which another club occupied the summit. To put it in perspective, only Ernesto Valverde has achieved a better percentage in Barcelona’s history. The former manager recorded an 84% leadership rate, finishing 80 of his 95 matchdays at the top between 2017 and 2020. Flick is setting new standards at Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) In terms of absolute numbers, Flick already ranks fourth among Barcelona managers, with Pep Guardiola leading the historical ranking with 87 occasions at the summit, followed by Frank Rijkaard with 85 and Valverde with 80. Barcelona’s title-winning seasons explain Flick’s remarkable numbers Flick’s record has remained impressive across all three campaigns. During his first season, Barcelona led the standings on 31 of 38 matchdays, representing 82%. That figure dropped to 26 occasions in 2025/26, equivalent to 69%, but the team still secured another championship. His current campaign has been even more dominant, as Barcelona have occupied first place on 11 of the 12 matchdays, giving Flick a 92% leadership rate in 2026/27. Flick guaranteed another week at the top of La Liga Flick enjoys a view from the top of La Liga table. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Barcelona’s position also means Flick is assured of extending his record after the international break. On that note, he will reach 69 leadership occasions across 89 matchdays regardless of the result against Villarreal when club football resumes. Barcelona currently have 33 points, three more than Real Madrid and five ahead of Atletico Madrid. Even a defeat at home to Villarreal would not automatically cost them first place, with their superior overall goal difference providing an additional advantage over Real Madrid.

top.title: ‘Who’s teaching him?’- Robert Horry tears into Walker Kessler’s offensive game with brutal assessment
top.description: Photo by Ben Liebenberg/Getty Images Robert Horry has delivered a brutal assessment of Walker Kessler’s offensive game, questioning the Lakers centre’s lack of post moves despite his seven-foot frame. Kessler has become an important part of Los Angeles’ strong start to the season after joining from the Utah Jazz. Luka Doncic backed the move, with the Lakers viewing the centre as someone who could fit their long-term plans. However, Horry believes there is plenty of room for improvement in Kessler’s work around the basket, particularly when it comes to creating his own shots. Robert Horry questions Walker Kessler’s lack of post moves Speaking on his Big Shot Bob podcast, the former Lakers star did not hold back when discussing the 24-year-old’s offensive limitations. “You know what’s really scary about Walker Kessler? Hey, I know guys in elementary got better post moves than him. He got no post moves, man. I’m like, who is teaching this dude any post moves? You’re seven f****** feet tall. Get you a little jump hook, man. You don’t have to dunk everything.” Horry also questioned Kessler’s tendency to pass out of offensive rebounds rather than take the opportunity to score himself. “I don’t even think he wants to score ’cause I’ve seen him get offensive rebounds and kick that out instead of crunching that. I’m like, dude, you’re 7 ft tall. Get you a power dribble. Go up and dunk that too.” The criticism comes despite Kessler settling into a role that the Lakers specifically brought him in to fill. Los Angeles wanted a centre who could protect the paint, defend around the rim and provide an option for easy finishes alongside Doncic. Kessler has helped deliver that, with the Lakers enjoying one of the best records in the NBA. His ability to play alongside Doncic and Austin Reaves has been an important part of their early-season success. Horry’s comments also overlook the way the modern NBA operates. Kessler is often expected to move the ball to better scorers rather than force attempts when Doncic or Reaves are available. With Kevon Looney struggling to provide a reliable alternative at centre, Kessler’s role remains particularly important. The Lakers will need him to maintain his defensive presence and continue fitting into their offence as they look to establish themselves as genuine Western Conference contenders. top.title: Two Dead, Several Injured As New York Building Collapses
top.description: Two people were killed Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said. Images from the scene showed firefighters sifting through a pile of rubble in front of what appeared to be a residential property with its walls torn down, exposing a bedroom and a clothing wardrobe. The building fell into a neighboring excavation site, trapping several people whom firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws. “We do not know how many people are still in the collapse zone, and this will be a prolonged operation,” FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore told reporters at the scene in Flatbush, Brooklyn late Wednesday. First responders tend to a collapsed building in Brooklyn in New York on November 11, 2026. She said two people had died, without disclosing their ages, and said 17 others were hurt, including seven children. Four people were critically injured. More than 250 firefighters and paramedics responded to the scene, the FDNY wrote on X, adding that the cause of the collapse was under investigation. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani praised the emergency services for their work, saying the site involved “precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface.” “I want to ask New Yorkers to please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss,” he added at a news conference. New York Fire Department Chief John Esposito speaks next to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani at a press conference after a building collapsed in Brooklyn in New York on November 11, 2026. One witness, named only as Anthony, told PIX11 News that he heard people screaming and a “bomb”-like noise as the building collapsed. Another witness, Melissa Orna, told The New York Times: “The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell.” The city’s Department of Buildings said its inspectors were on the scene “assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings.” Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of the department, said construction workers were performing excavation at the time of the collapse. He added that developers had plans approved for a three-story building at the site and were pursuing permission for a nine-story building. top.title: England's Blues brothers - how the Bellinghams helped save Birmingham
top.description: Jude Bellingham shared an old photo of him and brother Jobe after England's squad announcement last week [Jude Bellingham Instagram] It is six years since Jude Bellingham played his final game for Birmingham City, and three years since younger brother Jobe wore the club's shirt for the last time. While Jude, 23, is establishing himself as a footballing great at European greats Real Madrid following a spell at Borussia Dortmund, Jobe, 21, is continuing his football education at his brother's former club in Germany after two seasons with Sunderland. The Stourbridge-born midfielders have moved on with their careers. Their memories, however, live on at St Andrew's, such was the impact the boyhood Birmingham fans made in the Championship. On match days supporters stop and pose for photographs in front of Jude's mural outside the ground. Fans still turn up to matches wearing Bellingham shirts. "They both had a real connection with fans," Craig Courtney, from the Tilton Talk fan podcast, told BBC Sport. "Fans loved the fact they both cared. "They wore their hearts on their sleeves and helped Birmingham when we were fighting relegation. Even now, Jude and Jobe remember where it all started for them." The brothers played 70 league and cup games between them for Birmingham after graduating from the academy. They have never appeared together in a senior match, however, as Jude - who joined Birmingham aged eight - had left by the time Jobe broke into the first team in 2022. That could all change on Thursday. The Bellinghams will become the first brothers to play for England for 19 years if Jobe wins his first cap and appears alongside Jude, a veteran of 60 appearances, in the Nations League game with Croatia at Wembley. "It will be an incredibly proud moment for Birmingham City if that happens," said Courtney. 'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up Listen: How Jude Bellingham became a global brand 'Jude chose best way to look after Blues' Birmingham supporters have had little to cheer about recently. It is 15 years since they last appeared in the Premier League, while the 2011 League Cup winners even dipped down to League One recently. While fierce rivals Aston Villa were playing - and beating - Bayern Munich and Bologna in the Champions League two years ago, Birmingham were losing at Shrewsbury and drawing with Northampton Town. Yet the mood is changing at St Andrew's. After 15 games Birmingham sit top of the Championship and there are plans for a new 62,000-capacity stadium in time for 2030-31. "As a club, we've been right down in the doldrums," added Courtney. "Now we're top of the table and having a new stadium built. "There is an argument that none of this would have been possible without the fees received for Jude and Jobe." Despite club captain Reece James remaining sidelined through injury , the former Lyon defender has not started a Premier League fixture since September 12. Instead, academy graduate Acheampong has increasingly been favoured on the right side of the backline. Limited minutes spark departure speculation Signed from his boyhood French club Lyon for a fee of around £26m back in 2023, the attacking full-back had previously been a regular fixture in the capital, racking up 144 appearances and scoring three goals across all competitions. However, he has been named in the starting XI for just three of his seven top-flight outings during the current campaign. Aside from those sporadic league minutes, the defender started all three of his side's Carabao Cup ties before their fourth-round penalty shootout elimination against Liverpool. That reduced involvement has alerted domestic rivals, with City having already explored a potential move over the summer in hopes of sealing a reunion between the player and former Stamford Bridge boss Enzo Maresca. Financial verdict complicates Etihad pursuit Although the Etihad Stadium hierarchy remain keen admirers of his profile, the broadcaster notes that their ability to finance a £75m deal is complicated by ongoing off-field regulatory proceedings. Maresca's side are still awaiting the final outcome of their appeal after being found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules. An independent commission adjudged that the club had artificially inflated their revenue by £900m via 'sham' contracts over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. With a decisive sanctions hearing still pending and the result of their legal challenge yet to be confirmed, any pursuit of a big-money signing in the upcoming market is far from straightforward. Managerial transition clouds winter approach Meanwhile, United find themselves at a crossroads at Old Trafford after agreeing a deal in principle for United States boss Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick . Given that impending dugout change and City's ongoing legal battle, it remains unclear whether either suitor will lodge an official approach when the January window opens. Nevertheless, Gusto's situation will be watched closely if he remains out of favour.

top.title: 'I'd tape it to my thumb': Ex-Australia star admits to using sandpaper after Usman Khawaja's revelations - WATCH
top.description: The Sandpapergate controversy has resurfaced in Australian cricket, eight years after the 2018 scandal. Following fresh revelations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his memoir, 'Sabr', ex-leg-spinner Stuart MacGill has now admitted to using sandpaper on the ball during his playing career. MacGill, who played 44 Tests and three ODIs for Australia between 1998 and 2008, said he had used sandpaper on the ball but insisted that it was not part of a bigger plan to cheat. His admission has added another twist to the Sandpapergate controversy, which took place during Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. The incident had led to bans for three Australian players and remains one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket. MacGill reveals how he used sandpaper Speaking to former Sydney Sixers teammates Steve O'Keefe and Moises Henriques on a FanaticsTV YouTube show, MacGill explained how he would attach a small piece of sandpaper to his thumb and use it to scratch the ball. "I'd cut a small piece of sandpaper and tape it to my thumb," he said. "It was not a part of a massive 'global cheating scam'; I was just really curious to see what would happen and if it would work. And oh, it works (laughs)," said MacGill. He also explained how he would use the sandpaper after tea, remove it from his thumb and throw it away before the match continued. "What they would do is the umpires as you're walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there and you'd run out on the field, pick it up and go on the field. I would tape a little bit of a square of sandpaper on my thumb, pick the ball up just after tea, scratch the living daylights out of it, pull the sandpaper off, chuck it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. So nobody even knew that I'd done it, apart from all the scratches on the ball," he added. — thefanatics (@thefanatics) Khawaja's claims reopen Sandpapergate MacGill's admission comes after Khawaja made fresh claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in his memoir, 'Sabr'. Cricket Australia has maintained that the wider Australian team was not aware of the plan to use sandpaper to change the condition of the ball during the Cape Town Test against South Africa. However, Khawaja's revelations have raised fresh questions about what other players knew about the incident. Darren Lehmann, who was Australia's head coach during the 2018 tour of South Africa, has strongly denied knowing about the plan to use sandpaper. Players such as Mitchell Starc have also publicly denied any involvement in the scandal. Former Australia captain David Warner, one of the three players punished over the incident, has backed Khawaja and said that the claims in his autobiography are true.

Internal hire With over 40,000 employees, Nvidia could opt to go with an in-house pick to take the helm, including one of Huang’s dozens of direct reports. Tech publications frequently cited Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as an easy choice, if for no other reason than she is already among top leadership at the chip behemoth. Another longtime Nvidia honcho is Ian Buck, who oversees the company’s data center clients. He was a key mind behind the software that keeps Nvidia-designed chips in demand. Business magazine Inc. also lists Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, as a possible pick. A family affair Huang could also try and position a member of his own family as his replacement, with more than one option for a bloodline succession. His daughter Madison Huang is currently the senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and is among the names most suggested by analysts. As a marketing leader, she had a multi-year stint at luxury conglomerate LVMH. Jensen Huang’s son Spencer Huang could also be a potential successor. He currently works at Nvidia as the director of product management in the company’s robotics division. Huang’s cousin, Lisa Su, could also be a viable candidate for selection – not only is she his first cousin, once removed, but she also has valuable expertise as the longtime CEO of semiconductor giant AMD. Tech CEO swap Su is not the only tech chief being bandied around as a possible replacement for Huang. Rene Haas, CEO of UK chip design firm Arm, is another candidate being suggested by the tech press. Speculation runs wide in Silicon Valley, where former Apple CEO Tim Cook – who stepped down from leading the tech giant in August after 15 years at the helm – is another person insiders say could potentially be tapped. nigeria.description: By Adesina Wahab Parents under the aegis of National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, NAPTAN, and the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, have offered tips on how to stop the practice of students benefitting from the Student Loan Scheme and still going ahead to collect tuition fees from their parents and guardians. The practice, labelled double dipping by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, which gives out the loans, is gradually becoming rampant and erasing the main reason the loan scheme was initiated – take the burden of tuition payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Speaking with Thursday Learning, the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of NAPTAN, Chief Deolu Ogunbanjo, opined that such a practice negates the reason for the setting up of the scheme. “The Student Loan Scheme was set up to give access to higher education to students who would otherwise drop out because of inability to pay fees. It is also to take the burden of fee payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Such happenings may not be totally eradicated. We know how rascally some young ones can be. “I think the way out is to let the parents and guardians be aware when payments are made by NELFUND to beneficiaries. Let there be a means of notifying the parents that their children have benefitted from the scheme,” he said Similarly, the National Public Relations Officer of NANS, Comrade Obidah David, also supported notification being sent to parents of beneficiaries. “If it is a text message, they can send to parents and guardians of beneficiaries. Information on contacts of parents is always provided by students when registering. That is necessary in case of any emergency. Also, names of beneficiaries can be published whether in the traditional media or social media. There is nothing bad in that. It is for transparency, “ he stated. Recall that recently, the Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, said during a press briefing that the fund had identified cases of students allegedly accessing loan support while continuing to place the burden of tuition payments on their parents. Describing the practice as unacceptable, Sawyerr said the fund was determined to end the situation and strengthen transparency in the administration of the scheme. “This comment is based on our recognition that there are so many students out there who are double-dipping. Under the proposed arrangement, parents would be able to confirm whether their children’s school fees had been paid through NELFUND without necessarily having access to the actual amount involved. nigeria.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 12, 2026
nigeria.description: The Nigerian naira opened trading on Thursday, November 12, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, maintaining the wider spread observed earlier in the week. At the official window, data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the naira entering Thursday’s session around the ₦1,350.36 to ₦1,353.50 per dollar band. Early Thursday morning international currency feeds recorded spot quotes hovering near ₦1,345.72 per dollar, while official NFEM benchmarks reflect the closing figures from the prior trading session pending the day’s official fixing. Earlier in the week, trading at the official window saw intraday fluctuations between ₦1,349.25 and ₦1,354 per dollar, with interbank turnover reaching $248.07 million across 144 deals. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a significant discount to the official rate. Currency dealers across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,411 and ₦1,420 for buying, while selling rates ranged from ₦1,419 to ₦1,430 per dollar depending on transaction volume and location. This leaves an exchange rate gap of roughly ₦68 to ₦80 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and street-level rates. Market analysts attribute the recent softening of the local currency to heightened seasonal foreign exchange demand from importers and travelers heading into the end-of-year period, alongside foreign portfolio investment outflows and a firmer US dollar globally. Despite the recent dip—which saw the parallel market touch a 10-month low of ₦1,430 per dollar this week—Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain sturdy at approximately $54.9 billion, well above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion, offering a substantial buffer to support market liquidity through the remainder of the fourth quarter. nigeria.title: 4 dead, many hospitalised in Benue after consuming herbal mixture
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru Makurdi —No fewer than four persons have reportedly died, while 14 others are battling for their lives in hospital after allegedly consuming a suspected poisonous herbal mixture purchased in Oju township, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. It was gathered that the incident occurred after three men, identified as Magani, Mohamed and Kala, allegedly sold herbal preparations suspected to contain poisonous substances to residents of the Igede community during the Ihiejwo market day in Oju township, last weekend. According to the eyewitness, “The development gained attention when some of those, who drank the mixture and their loved ones raised the alarm on November 2, 2026, after several residents, who had purchased and consumed the herbal preparations started developing similar symptoms. “While the first victim reportedly died Tuesday morning, the second died in the early hours of Wednesday, and the third and fourth victims died later on November 4, 2026. “As we speak, over 14 other victims are currently battling for their lives, with many of them said to be in critical condition.” He disclosed that the three suspects allegedly involved in the sale of the herbal mixture were apprehended by the leadership of the Igede Youth Council, in collaboration with the Oju Local Government Area Township Youth leadership, and subsequently handed over to the police in Oju. “We have been told that the Oju Divisional Police Headquarters has transferred the case to the Benue State Police Command, where the suspects are currently undergoing investigation,” he said. Speaking while handing over the suspects to the police, President of the Igede Youth Council, John-Frank Ozzidi, called on the Benue State government to ensure a thorough investigation of the incident and guarantee that justice was served. Ozzidi said the Igede youths had deliberately refrained from taking the law into their hands, resisting the temptation to subject the suspects to jungle justice. He explained that their decision to allow the law to take its course demonstrated their confidence in the state government to ensure justice is done in the matter. The youth leader also urged political officeholders from the area to follow up on the case to ensure that the deceased victims got justice and that the circumstances surrounding the suspected poisoning were fully established. Contacted, the Chairman of Oju council, Mr. Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident but said he was yet to obtain the exact number of fatalities. nigeria.description: By YVONNE-FAITH ELAIGWU The history of payments is, in many ways, the history of making value easier to move. We started at barter and are now at electronic transfers, with stablecoins suggesting that the next evolution is here. New payment methods rarely make their predecessors useless. Cash did not immediately eliminate barter. Cards did not eliminate cheques. Account-to-account payments will not eliminate cards. But payments evolve. And one of the most interesting examples of that evolution can be found in an unlikely comparison: Nigeria and the United States. The United States built perhaps the world’s greatest card ecosystem. Nigeria just seems to have built past it. The American card system is extraordinary. Over decades, the U.S. built an ecosystem connecting consumers, merchants, issuing banks, acquiring banks, and card networks. Around it grew credit bureaus, credit scores, revolving credit, chargebacks, fraud protection, loyalty points, airline miles, and billions of dollars of rewards. Consequently, Americans have a compelling reason to use cards. And use them, they do. Walk into an American store, and the natural question is still: Which card am I using? Nigeria never developed America’s deep credit-card culture. Debit cards became widespread, but cards did not become as deeply embedded in the country’s economic architecture as they did in America. Instead, Nigeria increasingly solved digital payments at the bank-account level. At the centre of this transformation is the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System and its NIBSS Instant Payment platform, built to operate 24/7 with most transactions settling in under one second. This infrastructure changed behaviour. Any individual or company can pay another individual or merchant, and the transaction can be executed on a Friday evening or a Sunday morning. The expectation is still remarkably simple: the money should arrive now. That expectation is one of Nigeria’s greatest payment achievements. America’s success may be part of its problem. nigeria.title: Right-sizing the map of Africa
nigeria.description: The United Nations General Assembly has, for the first time, formally endorsed a global shift away from the centuries-old Mercator map in favour of projections that show Africa—and other equatorial regions—in their true relative size. This “Correct the Map” resolution, spearheaded by Togo on behalf of the African Group and backed by the African Union, passed by 164 votes to one, with six abstentions. While non-binding, it marks a watershed moment in how the world visually represents the continent—and, by extension, how it perceives Africa’s weight in global affairs. The root of the misrepresentation lies in the Mercator projection, devised in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator for maritime navigation. To keep compass bearings straight, Mercator preserved angles and shapes—but at the cost of area. The result: landmasses near the poles, such as Europe, North America and Greenland, are visually enlarged, while those near the equator, including Africa, Latin America and South Asia, are shrunk. On typical Mercator wall maps, Greenland appears roughly the same size as Africa. In reality, Africa covers about 30.3 million square kilometres, making it around 14 times larger than Greenland’s 2.1 million square kilometres. This is not a minor quirk; it is a systematic visual bias baked into the most widely used world map for nearly five centuries. The resolution encourages governments, schools, international organisations, media houses and technology companies to adopt equal-area projections, especially the Equal Earth projection, whenever comparative continental size matters. It frames map distortion as more than a technical issue—calling it a cognitive, educational, cultural and geopolitical problem that has contributed to the symbolic minimisation of Africa in the global imagination. While symbolic correction matters, Africa’s greatest vulnerabilities lie in structural exploitation and escalating insecurity, notably from Islamist insurgencies across the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin and parts of the Horn. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. (Photo by Chris Lee - Chelsea FC/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) | Chelsea FC via Getty Images We’re slowly approaching the January transfer window, and given that it’s the international break, there’s plenty of space for a few rumors to make their way around the footballverse. Of particular interest to us may be the story that Malo Gusto is said to be “open” to leaving Chelsea and is now “assessing his options” with three and half years still to run on his current contract (2030 expiry). The BBC are among those who nibbled a bit at this little rumor-nugget, adding that while Chelsea’s stance at the moment is “unclear”, we were shopping the 23-year-old around this summer already, at a £75m asking price. That’s a rather optimistic valuation, especially now that Manchester City cannot just make up income numbers (or can they?). Enzo Maresca was always a big fan of Gusto, and a reunion was speculated about before the season, but unlike in the case of Enzo Fernández, did not come to fruition. It probably won’t help Gusto’s valuation that he’s finding himself less and less involved as the season’s come along. He’s not started a league match for two months, and I don’t imagine too many are questioning those decisions from Xabi Alonso, unlike some of his other choices of late. Gusto’s substitute appearance against Sunderland was his 100th Premier League appearance, and 144th overall for Chelsea. He’s among our longest-serving players these days despite his young age — a testament to the constant chopping and changing of the team. Only Reece James and Wesley Fofana have been part of the first-team squad for longer. But throughout those 3.5 years, Gusto has failed to convince consistently, despite his versatility and world class speed. He’s had moments of great impact and could at times even be practically unplayable for the opposition with his fluid movement and lack of a defined position. But those moments have been few and far between. His best season for us was, perhaps, his very first, when he often thrived in Mauricio Pochettino’s chaosball. Since Poch is about to take over at Manchester United, perhaps they will be interested in another Chelsea castoff? Malo Gusto is open to a move away in January. sports.title: Hansi Flick achieves remarkable La Liga record as Barcelona dominate title race
sports.description: Hansi Flick achieves remarkable La Liga record as Barcelona dominate title race Hansi Flick has established an extraordinary level of consistency in La Liga, spending 68 of the 88 matchdays he has overseen as Barcelona manager at the top of the table. According to figures published by AS , the German has occupied first place for approximately 77% of his league tenure, placing him among the most successful Barcelona managers in the competition’s history. His dominance has coincided with two consecutive La Liga titles in 2024/25 and 2025/26, and now, with Barcelona also leading the 2026/27 standings after 12 matches, Flick is positioning himself for another championship. Flick’s La Liga dominance puts him among Barcelona’s greats The outlet affirms that of the 88 league matchdays under his management, his team have finished in first place on 68 occasions, leaving just 20 matchdays in which another club occupied the summit. To put it in perspective, only Ernesto Valverde has achieved a better percentage in Barcelona’s history. The former manager recorded an 84% leadership rate, finishing 80 of his 95 matchdays at the top between 2017 and 2020. Flick is setting new standards at Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) In terms of absolute numbers, Flick already ranks fourth among Barcelona managers, with Pep Guardiola leading the historical ranking with 87 occasions at the summit, followed by Frank Rijkaard with 85 and Valverde with 80. Barcelona’s title-winning seasons explain Flick’s remarkable numbers Flick’s record has remained impressive across all three campaigns. During his first season, Barcelona led the standings on 31 of 38 matchdays, representing 82%. That figure dropped to 26 occasions in 2025/26, equivalent to 69%, but the team still secured another championship. His current campaign has been even more dominant, as Barcelona have occupied first place on 11 of the 12 matchdays, giving Flick a 92% leadership rate in 2026/27. Flick guaranteed another week at the top of La Liga Flick enjoys a view from the top of La Liga table. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Barcelona’s position also means Flick is assured of extending his record after the international break. On that note, he will reach 69 leadership occasions across 89 matchdays regardless of the result against Villarreal when club football resumes. Barcelona currently have 33 points, three more than Real Madrid and five ahead of Atletico Madrid. Even a defeat at home to Villarreal would not automatically cost them first place, with their superior overall goal difference providing an additional advantage over Real Madrid.

Luka Doncic backed the move, with the Lakers viewing the centre as someone who could fit their long-term plans. Kessler is often expected to move the ball to better scorers rather than force attempts when Doncic or Reaves are available. With Kevon Looney struggling to provide a reliable alternative at centre, Kessler’s role remains particularly important. The Lakers will need him to maintain his defensive presence and continue fitting into their offence as they look to establish themselves as genuine Western Conference contenders. Rivals monitor sidelined French full-back According to talkSPORT , both north-west heavyweights are tracking Gusto closely after his first-team opportunities diminished under the Blues' new Spanish tactician. Despite club captain Reece James remaining sidelined through injury , the former Lyon defender has not started a Premier League fixture since September 12. Instead, academy graduate Acheampong has increasingly been favoured on the right side of the backline. Limited minutes spark departure speculation Signed from his boyhood French club Lyon for a fee of around £26m back in 2023, the attacking full-back had previously been a regular fixture in the capital, racking up 144 appearances and scoring three goals across all competitions. However, he has been named in the starting XI for just three of his seven top-flight outings during the current campaign. sports.title: 'I'd tape it to my thumb': Ex-Australia star admits to using sandpaper after Usman Khawaja's revelations - WATCH
sports.description: The Sandpapergate controversy has resurfaced in Australian cricket, eight years after the 2018 scandal. Following fresh revelations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his memoir, 'Sabr', ex-leg-spinner Stuart MacGill has now admitted to using sandpaper on the ball during his playing career. MacGill, who played 44 Tests and three ODIs for Australia between 1998 and 2008, said he had used sandpaper on the ball but insisted that it was not part of a bigger plan to cheat. His admission has added another twist to the Sandpapergate controversy, which took place during Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. The incident had led to bans for three Australian players and remains one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket. MacGill reveals how he used sandpaper Speaking to former Sydney Sixers teammates Steve O'Keefe and Moises Henriques on a FanaticsTV YouTube show, MacGill explained how he would attach a small piece of sandpaper to his thumb and use it to scratch the ball. "I'd cut a small piece of sandpaper and tape it to my thumb," he said. "It was not a part of a massive 'global cheating scam'; I was just really curious to see what would happen and if it would work. And oh, it works (laughs)," said MacGill. He also explained how he would use the sandpaper after tea, remove it from his thumb and throw it away before the match continued. "What they would do is the umpires as you're walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there and you'd run out on the field, pick it up and go on the field. I would tape a little bit of a square of sandpaper on my thumb, pick the ball up just after tea, scratch the living daylights out of it, pull the sandpaper off, chuck it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. So nobody even knew that I'd done it, apart from all the scratches on the ball," he added. — thefanatics (@thefanatics) Khawaja's claims reopen Sandpapergate MacGill's admission comes after Khawaja made fresh claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in his memoir, 'Sabr'. Cricket Australia has maintained that the wider Australian team was not aware of the plan to use sandpaper to change the condition of the ball during the Cape Town Test against South Africa. However, Khawaja's revelations have raised fresh questions about what other players knew about the incident. Darren Lehmann, who was Australia's head coach during the 2018 tour of South Africa, has strongly denied knowing about the plan to use sandpaper. Players such as Mitchell Starc have also publicly denied any involvement in the scandal. Former Australia captain David Warner, one of the three players punished over the incident, has backed Khawaja and said that the claims in his autobiography are true.

technology.title: AWS distills its cloud into a local emulator that runs on your PC
technology.description: AWS has released an emulator that kind-of-almost lets you use its cloud on a PC. As explained in the GitHub repository for the prosaically named “AWS Emulator,” the tool “is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint.” The emulator doesn’t replicate the whole AWS cloud, instead offering its APIs. “You use it to test your software without calling AWS, on your own machine, on a development server, or in continuous integration (CI),” the repo explains. Because those tests never touch the AWS cloud, the tool is free to use. AWS wrote the emulator in Rust, a choice that senior specialist solutions architect Daniel Abib wrote helps to ensure the tool “stays light on CPU and memory on a laptop.” The emulator tool doesn’t replicate the entire AWS cloud. Abib said it supports the APIs of AWS services that have an API model in the AWS API models repository on GitHub . The Register found over 1,300 items on that page. While the tool lets developers test APIs, it doesn’t replicate anywhere near all the features of the Amazonian cloud. “It doesn’t evaluate IAM [Identity and Access Management] policies the way AWS does, and each emulator acts as a single account, with no cross-account or cross-Region behavior,” Abib wrote, adding “How closely it matches AWS varies by service and feature.” AWS publishes “fidelity scores” that detail how closely the emulator works on different AWS services. Amazon tries to achieve full fidelity, so the emulator produces the same results as AWS for valid API calls, and the same errors for invalid ones. Coding agents can also drive the Emulator, an option The Register mentions because AWS advises the easiest way to check if a project will work with the tool is to use the aws-emulator skill for AI coding agents. “With the skill, your agent finds the AWS operations and resources that your project depends on. It checks them against the fidelity tests and fidelity scores for the emulator. It then tells you which parts of your project you can rely on the emulator for, and which ones might behave differently from AWS,” according to AWS documentation. AWS has made the emulator available as an RPM or Debian package. Mac and PC users will need to run Docker and an image of the Emulator. “You install the emulator, start it, and point your tools at the local endpoint,” Abib instructed. “When AWS Emulator starts, it generates its own credentials, a config file, and a certificate, and writes them to ~/.aws/emulator/9297/ . You set environment variables so the AWS SDK talks to your laptop instead of AWS, and your application code stays unchanged.” “From there, your existing tests, CLI scripts, and coding agents keep working the way they already do. A unit test that creates an Amazon DynamoDB table, writes an item, and reads it back is the same test, and it runs on your machine without a deployment.” The cloud colossus’s intent appears, as ever, to encourage more use of its cloud – in this case by satisfying developers their code will run w

technology.title: Disgraced former CA eMudhra blames buggy script for hopelessly weak certificates
technology.description: Former certification authority eMudhra has claimed a buggy Python script is the main reason it issued laughably insecure digital certificates. The company posted its account of the matter on Bugzilla where a user with the handle “Naveen Kumar ML” wrote “During a single key‑generation ceremony on 30 April 2025, sixteen subordinate (issuing) CA key pairs in eMudhra’s ‘B’ and ‘C’ series were generated correctly on a hardware security module and then processed through an approved wrap/unwrap round‑trip using a custom python key‑handling script.” eMudhra aimed to create eight ECDSA P-384 private keys which should have been 48 bytes long. But the script contained what Kumar described as “a bug/defect in the import code [which] resulted in a read‑back from the unwrapped object that truncated the private value, so the certified public keys correspond to private scalars below the expected range and are recoverable from public information.” The truncation is the key problem here, because it appears that eMudhra ignored 47 of the 48 bytes, producing its infamously insecure single-byte keys such as the number four. Whatever the nature of the bug, Kumar asserts it was “a custom script run only on an isolated ceremony host and was not a function of the emCA software.” eMudhra needed that script because “global supply chain constraints” meant it couldn’t acquire the hardware security modules (HSMs), devices that generate and store cryptographic keys, that it wanted to use when creating a set of certificates for use in the USA. It therefore used HSMs made by a company called Utimaco to generate keys and planned to transfer the keys it produced to a different set of HSMs from a company called Crypto4A. Kumar explained that eMudhra decided on that move, which is unusual, because changes to policy about provenance of certificates meant it had to generate new certs by the end of May. The plan went sour when the company didn’t notice the errors in its script and didn’t test the keys it created. The rest is history: a Mozilla team member noticed that the company’s keys were woefully weak and pointed out that attackers could therefore issue fraudulent certificates that allowed them to impersonate servers, observe traffic, or even modify data in transit. Browser-makers quickly tweaked their software so it would not recognize certs from eMudhra. The Indian business then quit the SSL/TLS certification business, which it said was never a major source of revenue but had suddenly become a severe source of embarrassment. Kumar’s new post lists three steps eMudhra will take to wind up its certification business, one of which will see the company “Put in place improvements motivated by findings of [an] independent review to strengthen our general PKI operations.” Sounds like a plan. ®

technology.title: Russian cloud Yandex says drone attacks on its datacenters caused data loss
technology.description: Russian cloud operator Yandex has admitted to data loss after a drone attack on one of its datacenters. The attack, which Ukrainian press said was ordered by Kyiv, happened in early October and caused a fire and subsequent outage at Yandex’s ru-central1-b availability zone. Subsequent strikes targeted more Yandex datacenters and disrupted more of the company’s cloud and payment services. On Tuesday, Yandex posted an update on its recovery efforts, which it spun as something of a triumph because it restored over 97 percent of customer data. Of course that also means the company lost 2.84 percent of customer data, which it blamed on “critical hardware damage and a lack of backups on the platform.” It’s unclear if Yandex’s use of the phrase “on the platform” indicates it doesn’t keep backups of its own cloud, if whatever resilience techniques it employs don’t create multiple copies of customer data, or if clients didn’t protect their data. Whatever happened, Yandex has decided to enable backups by default for all VMs customers create in its cloud. That decision will mean customers will consume and pay for more Yandex resources, unless they opt out of the automated backups. Given that drones damaged three Yandex locations, and the war with Ukraine continues, users have good reasons to consider alternatives to its services. Indeed, Yandex’s announcement of its recovery efforts links to a page extolling the virtues of a hybrid cloud when devising data protection strategies. That page also mentions Yandex’s own Stackland product, which brings its stack on-prem, as an example of a hybrid approach. On Wednesday the company also launched a new availability zone named ru-central1-f. Yandex didn’t say where it’s located, other than to say it’s in “a new location.” Interestingly, Yandex has imposed quotas that limit the amount of resources users can access in the new availability zone and says it can’t yet handle traffic to private endpoints at the new facility. Many nations have imposed sanctions that restrict sales of technology products to Russia. It’s therefore unsurprising that Yandex might struggle to provision enough infrastructure to allow untrammeled access to a new availability zone. ®

technology.title: US bit barn boom sees energy needs grow 10x as fast as grid capacity
technology.description: Datacenter power consumption in the US is growing roughly ten times faster than grid capacity, meaning facilities may soon need to find a large chunk of their own electricity from other sources. Surging demand for AI infrastructure is driving a wave of new server farms across America, but it is exposing long-term underinvestment in the grid networks required to deliver power where it's needed. Insurance broker Howden calculates that datacenters would need to source up to 58 percent of their power off the grid by 2030 just to keep their share of grid capacity from growing. Gartner warned in June that the energy consumed by AI datacenters is on track to grow 26 percent this year, and grid supply may be unable to keep pace with demand by the end of this decade. Howden's analysis of data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and S&P Global found that since the year 2000, power being fed to data campuses has risen 19 percent a year on average, while the electricity grid expanded capacity by just 2 percent per annum over the same period. Datacenters' share of US grid capacity was circa five percent in 2025, up from 0.1 percent in 2000 – a 50-fold increase. Management consultancy Bain & Company issued a report two years ago warning that energy companies must switch gear and invest in building out grid capacity faster , as energy draw by server farms is expected to more than double by 2030. This doesn't mean that datacenters are in danger of eating all of America's electricity, at least not in the immediate future. The graph makes it appear that the two lines are about to cross, but the chart uses different scales: 1,400 gigawatts on the left axis for grid capacity, versus just 80 on the right for datacenters. Keeping datacenters at five percent of grid capacity requires 110 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity by 2030, Howden estimates – an expansion it considers unlikely. Instead, it expects a combination of greater reliance on the grid, slower development at power-constrained sites, and alternative supplies. For the largest, most power-constrained projects, Howden warns that grid delays of two to six years could mean $800 million to $2.4 billion in forgone revenue. "Power availability is becoming one of the defining challenges of the datacenter boom," says Howden head of Natural Resources Stuart Adam. As planets shift relative to fixed stars , they may appear from our perspective to get closer to other astronomical objects. Such meetings are called conjunctions . They don’t happen by chance, but follow the precise laws of celestial mechanics . This peaceful image , captured in Poland , shows the crescent Moon above the Tatra Mountains , and bright Venus close by, a little lower in the horizon. It was found in 1890 that Spica is a binary star: two massive blue stars orbiting each other every 4 days. But earlier this year it was reported that Spica, the current companion of wandering Venus, is actually a triple system . Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? science.title: Scotland’s Flow Country
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Scotland’s Flow Country Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search March 4, 2024 Compared to ecosystems in many other parts of the world, the blanket bogs of the Flow Country in northern Scotland are unassuming—soggy, treeless landscapes dominated by hummocky mosses, grasses, and heathers. Yet, to ecologists, the seemingly desolate areas are nothing short of extraordinary. The bogs store tremendous quantities of carbon . That’s because their soils are so waterlogged that microbes cannot fully break down dead plant material, a process that would otherwise release carbon dioxide. Instead, partially decayed plant matter accumulates into thick layers of spongy, crumbly, carbon-rich material called peat . The unusual ecosystems, also called blanket mires and featherbed bogs, only occur in places with abundant rainfall, poor drainage, and low levels of evapotranspiration . These types of bogs cover just 120,000 square kilometers (46,000 square miles) globally, less than one-tenth of one percent of Earth’s land surface. The image above, captured by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 , is centered on blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands, home to the largest such ecosystem in Europe. This peatland is also the first of its type to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site . The peat bogs of northern Scotland, home to more than 30 species of sphagnum moss , are spread across some 1,900 square kilometers (730 square miles) of the country’s Highlands region. In this image, boggy areas appear dark brown and are sprinkled with lakes. The light green area on the right side around Thurso is farmland. The darker green geometric patterns in the center are conifer plantations . The image was captured in the spring, the part of the year when the land surface is most waterlogged and peat bogs begin to accumulate large amounts of new biomass. While forests store most of their carbon in living trees—which eventually release it back into the atmosphere when they burn or die—peat bogs often store carbon for many thousands of years. Some parts of the Flow Country have been accumulating peat for more than 9,000 years, building deposits exceeding eight meters thick, according to UNESCO. Overall, scientists estimate that all of the world’s peatlands cover just 3 percent of Earth’s land surface but store more than 600 gigatons of carbon—about twice as much as all the world’s forests combined. science.title: Some PFAS chemicals are declining in English rivers but others are appearing
science.description: The River Wye in Derbyshire, England Dave Porter/Alamy The concentration of two of the most well-studied PFAS forever chemicals are showing a strong downward trend in English rivers. The finding adds to a mixed story for the power of global restrictions. The levels of perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in English rivers have fallen by 30 per cent and 29 per cent, respectively, over the past decade, according to a new report by scientists at the Environment Agency (EA) , a UK government green regulator. Both of these human-made chemicals take a long time to break down in the environment. The International Agency for Research on Cancer recently designated PFOA as carcinogenic to humans , and both forever chemicals have been linked to reproductive health and developmental impacts as well as other serious health issues. Advertisement Read more Fish-based pet food may expose cats and dogs to forever chemicals Under the United Nations Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, the use of PFOS was restricted from 2009, and the use of PFOA was restricted from 2019 – although there were country-specific caveats on which uses they applied to. They had both been used in non-stick coatings on consumer products as well as in industrial processes. Both were also used in firefighting foams, a major source of PFAS pollution entering the environment, with a ban on PFOA in firefighting foams only coming into force in the UK in 2025. Rob Bradburne , the EA’s chief scientist, describes his group’s results as proof that the global ban was “a really positive move”. But, he adds that the huge range of PFAS chemicals is going to “complicate the story”. An issue that is clear in the dataset for England is that while these two main PFAS have declined, many other “forever chemicals” that are being used to replace them – such as short-chain PFAS and fluorotelomer compounds – have now emerged in the environment at detectable levels. One of the short-chain PFAS that is now particularly widespread across the world is trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) – which can form when pesticides, refrigerants and pharmaceuticals break down in the environment. science.title: NASA kick-starts a fresh push to bring Mars samples home
science.description: null A long-term goal at NASA has been the ability to robotically haul back to Earth specimens from the Red Planet. NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for its troubled Mars Sample Return (MSR) program, called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture, or PSRA in space shorthand. The plan is to establish a fresh NASA strategy for gathering Mars samples collected by the Perseverance rover and launching them back to Earth. The PSRA initiative was noted on Nov. 9 by Tiffany Morgan, director of the NASA Mars Exploration Program (MEP), during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG). Here's the PSRA strategy: Develop impartial recommendations for retrieving the Martian samples collected by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover and deliver them to Earth Assess proposed mission requirements Review prior lessons learned Evaluate current capabilities and acquisition options Morgan noted that there will be a PSRA strategy team kickoff in January 2027 with a final report due in winter 2027-2028. Pick-me-ups The backdrop to the PSRA activity is that there's one busy rover already on the Red Planet snagging and bagging samples. NASA's Perseverance Mars rover remains on the prowl within Jezero Crater following its touchdown in February 2021. That car-sized robot has been grabbing select specimens from across the area and gingerly dropping the sealed pick-me-ups on the surface of Mars , as well as stuffing them inside the rover itself. Those collectibles may well hold signs of past life on the enigmatic, dusty and foreboding Red Planet. NASA and the European Space Agency have for years been intently plotting out plans to send future spacecraft to Mars and haul those Perseverance-plucked bits, pieces, and sniffs of atmosphere to Earth for rigorous inspection here on Earth using state-of-the-art equipment. science.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
science.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space. Catching one takes luck, as a telescope has to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right moment. That changed with CHIME (the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) in British Columbia. With a very wide field of view and a supercomputer to process its data, CHIME more than quadrupled the number of known FRBs in its first year of operation alone. Between 2018 and 2023, CHIME recorded 4,539 bursts from 3,641 sources. As pulses of radio waves, our eyes haven't evolved to see FRBs, nor can we hear them as they aren't sound waves. Well, not until now. "Artist and composer Andrew Melchior turned all of the CHIME bursts into sound for "The Logos," an installation that has played daily at Oulu Cathedral in Finland since early April and is scheduled to run through the end of the year. Melchior and Kiyoshi Masui, an associate professor of physics at MIT, "sonified" the bursts, translating data into acoustics so that human ears can hear them. The structure of each real signal is mapped to varying musical pitches and played through 12 loudspeakers spread throughout the cathedral. The result is a range of tones, with distant FRBs humming, rumbling, popping, and whistling. The signals are old by any human measure. According to a description on Melchior's website , the youngest in the work are about 50 million years old, and the oldest are about 8 to 9 billion years old. An animation shows the random appearance of fast radio bursts (FRBs) across the sky (Image credit: NRAO Outreach/T. Jarrett (IPAC/Caltech); B. Saxton, NRAO/AUI/NSF)) Physics also plays a role in what is heard. Each burst arrives with its high frequencies first and sweeps downward, stretched by its journey through intergalactic gas, "and you can hear that dispersion as it falls from the dome," Melchior told Space.com by email. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA launches Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day. The astronauts returned to Earth after four days in space. Both Aldrin and Lovell went on to join the Apollo program . Aldrin became the second person to walk on the moon during Apollo 11 , and Lovell became the commander of Apollo 13 . The Gemini 12 astronauts James Lovell and Edwin Aldrin lifted off aboard a Titan launch vehicle from the Kennedy Space Center on November 11, 1966, an hour and a half after their Agena target vehicle was orbited by an Atlas rocket. (Image credit: NASA/MSFC) Why it mattered Gemini 12 may have closed out NASA's Gemini program of two-person space missions, but it established the mission also established the fundamentals of spacewalking that Apollo astronauts would use when they walked on the moon. It's fitting that Aldrin was the primary spacewalker of the mission. A rookie astronaut (and the first to earn a Ph.D.), Aldrin set a precedent by training for his spacewalk in a neutral buoyancy pool in Maryland to better simulate working in weightlessness. Then he did it again as the second person to walk on the moon on Apollo 11. "This approach became so successful, underwater training has become the primary spacewalk training method used by the United State, Russia and China," NASA officials said in a mission overview . "Today, NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory in Houston is large enough to include mockups of major sections of the International Space Station . As such, it is the largest indoor body of water in the world, with 6.2 million gallons of water." science.title: Blood-thinning drug limits cartilage damage and relieves osteoarthritis pain
science.description: Coloured X-ray of osteoarthritis of the knee ALAIN POL/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY A drug that prevents blood clots reduced pain and improved mobility in mice and monkeys with knee osteoarthritis. The approach seems to partly work by reducing inflammatory signals that degrade cartilage. Osteoarthritis is caused by the wear and tear of cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, leading to inflammation, pain and stiffness. It affects more than 500 million people worldwide. Painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs can relieve symptoms, but no approved drugs halt or slow worsening of the disease. “We have nothing to offer our patients apart from suggesting weight loss, or offering drugs that provide pain relief,” says Tonia Vincent at the University of Oxford, who wasn’t involved in the study. Advertisement Read more The best non-drug therapies to relieve the pain of knee osteoarthritis It is widely thought that inflammatory molecules called TNF-alpha and IL-1-beta drive inflammation that worsens osteoarthritis. This has led to clinical trials testing drugs that target either of these molecules. But these have been unsuccessful, potentially because these molecules compensate for each other when one is blocked, according to Chuan-Ju Liu at Yale University and his colleagues. To explore whether targeting both molecules may be more effective, the researchers surgically removed part of the cartilage in the left knee joints of eight monkeys to mimic wear and tear that triggers osteoarthritis. A month later, four of the monkeys took a daily dose of a drug called dabigatran, mixed into their food. Dabigatran is commonly used to prevent blood clots in people at increased risk of strokes, but has also been shown to block inflammatory signals via both TNF-alpha and IL-1-beta. The remaining monkeys ate their usual food as a control. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter After seven months, MRI scans revealed that the left-knee cartilage in monkeys on dabigratan was about 60 per cent thicker, on average, compared to the control monkeys. This suggests that the drug reduced cartilage damage, slowing the progression of osteoarthritis, says Liu. Monkeys on dabigratan also had a roughly 15 per cent greater range of motion in their left knee than the control monkeys. “Monkeys receiving dabigatran showed a more natural walking pattern and a greater range of knee movement,” says Liu. “These improvements are consistent with reduced joint stiffness and discomfort.” In further experiments, the team confirmed their findings in mice with surgically-induced knee osteoarthritis, which also revealed that dabigratan reduced inflammation in the knee by about 60 per cent. science.title: Andy Weir's 'Exoplanet' just landed on Audible, but what actually makes an exoplanet habitable?
science.description: null Imagine you’ve crash-landed on an alien planet. Your ship is destroyed, your oxygen supply is dangerously low, and the landscape around you is completely unknown. Where would you begin looking for clues to your survival? Surprisingly, the best place to start could be the star overhead. This is the predicament that three crew members of the Wild Blue Yonder face in Audible’s new sci-fi thriller, "Exoplanet." This sci-fi thriller is written by acclaimed comic writer Benjamin Percy, executive produced by Andy Weir (Project Hail Mary, The Martian), and features an all-star voice cast including Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo . Stranded on an unfamiliar planet, they encounter volcanic wastelands, unknown skies, and environments that seem to defy reason. But behind the extraordinary events of this audio drama is a very real scientific question: what makes a planet habitable? Learning from the stars An artist's concept illustrates a young, red dwarf star surrounded by three planets. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) In “Exoplanet”, the crew view skies that are not only unfamiliar but also seemingly different from one another. One character sees a sun as so dim that he can look directly at it, while another suffers under a blazing heat, surrounded by stretches of sun-scorched red rock. For astronomers, the light emitted by a star is one of the most crucial tools for understanding planets orbiting it. Using a technique called spectroscopy , astronomers split starlight into its constituent wavelengths, producing a spectrum much like a rainbow. By studying this spectrum, they can investigate the temperature, composition, and other physical properties of the star. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) However, stellar temperature is only part of the picture. The amount of energy a planet receives depends on both the luminosity of the star and its orbital distance. Astronomers use these measurements to determine whether a world lies in the habitable zone of a star, where temperatures could allow liquid water to exist on the surface given a suitable atmosphere. A planet orbiting a cool red dwarf would need to be much closer to its star than Earth is to the Sun to be in this habitable zone. Unfortunately, being in this zone is no guarantee of a planetary paradise. Hostile stars Black holes are bad news for life, but living stars provide just as many problems. (Image credit: Audible) A planet that sits comfortably in the habitable zone is ultimately still at the mercy of its star. Stars emit more than just the light we see. Ultraviolet radiation and X-rays can interact with planetary atmospheres, altering chemistry and even contributing to the loss of the atmosphere . Violent stellar flares can produce bursts of high-energy radiation. A planet could offer a wonderfully balmy temperature, only to be bombarded with radiation from the host star. science.title: Who will step up to preserve space age artefacts for future generations?
science.description: NASA/JPL-Caltech Around 40,000 years from now, the Voyager 1 probe will pass within astronomical spitting distance of the star Gliese 445. From there, it will continue drifting through the universe on an endless journey that marks humanity’s first attempt to reach the stars. Voyager 1 – which on 18 November will have travelled one light day from Earth – began its odyssey almost 50 years ago, meaning it has been operating for the majority of the space age. That makes it a rarity: most of our iconic spacecraft ended their lives burned up in Earth’s atmosphere or in bits at the bottom of the ocean. Two of the most important missions still flying today, the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station, look set to share the same fate in the near future, even as scientists call for Hubble to be preserved . While some craft like the space shuttles are on display in museums, our present space history is, essentially, in its dark ages, with little thought currently given to preserving spacecraft in situ, where our space-travelling descendants may wish to marvel at them. Even the Apollo hardware left behind on the moon has almost no protection in international law. Advertisement Perhaps we need an organisation like the UNESCO World Heritage Committee to designate important space artefacts for preservation, and encourage funding from cultural and heritage budgets, not scientific ones, to do this. Of course, with such budgets often under threat and the US set to leave UNESCO at the end of this year, this could introduce new problems. Private philanthropy is another option. If humanity is to one day take its place among the stars, a fantasy that fuels many a tech billionaire, it would be a great shame to not be able to look back at how we got there. Just as we remember 19th-century captains of industry like Andrew Carnegie and J. P. Morgan for funding great cultural institutions, perhaps we should be lobbying for the creation of a Musk Space Museum or Bezos Orbital Institute.
